text:
emily-support: Heads-up — AcmeHealth filed an escalation after our canary rollout (deployed ~11:02 UTC). They report long-context behavior regression: instructions in the system prompt are being ignored or cut off mid-conversation, plus occasional 500s and latency spikes. Putting details below.

eng-ml-oncall: Thanks — can you paste a minimal repro and the model + variant they hit? Also any request ids / trace ids from their failing calls.

emily-support: Attaching their minimal repro. They used our chat endpoint with a long system prompt (~3.2k chars). Model reported in headers: model=redwood-large-v2, variant=fp16-optimized. Customer example:
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "redwood-large-v2",
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant that MUST follow the numbered rules below exactly:\n1) ALWAYS start replies with the string [ACME].\n2) If user asks for code, include a short example in python.\n3) Never make up policy text.\n ... (long policy continued, ~3200 chars)"},
    {"role":"user","content":"Generate onboarding checklist for new clinicians."}
  ],
  "max_tokens": 4000
}
```
Their returned value starts with normal text but later drops the rule and begins ignoring instructions:
```
[ACME] Sure, here is a checklist...
...
(OUTPUT LATE IN STREAM)
We recommend reviewing internal policies.

Note: The response does NOT include the python example requested and later the assistant starts providing hallucinated policy text.
```
They also saw a few requests that failed with 500 and latency jumps to ~1.2s per token during the canary window. Billing note: customer saw extra tokens due to retries.

jonathan-r: Do we have a rollout timestamp / revision? @deploy-bot please confirm which variant was routed to canary.

deploy-bot: Canary started at 2026-03-17T11:02:12Z, route policy: 10% traffic -> redwood-large-v2:fp16-optimized (kernel build b1527). Prior stable was redwood-large-v1:int8.

eng-ml-oncall: Possible leads: 1) variant changed KV cache eviction heuristics or chunking which shortens effective long-window; 2) tokenization change or context window mapping bug on the fp16 build; 3) fallback/partial decode due to internal oom leading to truncated tail behavior. Need server logs and the request_id for the failing calls.

maria-l: Customer impact looks high (esp. regulated content). Can we pause canary for this build until we have a clear repro and mitigations?

kevin-s: I pulled the canary traces I can access. I see a pattern: for multi-message requests with very large system prompts we hit a different auto-batching path that slices the prefix into frames. Latency spikes coincide with a retry loop where the runtime downgraded to a fallback kernel, which then appears to truncate cached KV entries earlier than the stable variant. Attaching inline snippet of the relevant log lines (anonymized):
```
[11:02:15.231] request_id=rx-9f2a kernel=fused-attn-v2 fallback=true kv_cache_max_seq=2048 prefix_chunks=3
[11:02:15.234] request_id=rx-9f2a error=partial_output_evicted
[11:02:15.235] request_id=rx-9f2a retrying with kernel=attn-compat seq_limit=1024
```

eng-ml-oncall: That log matches the symptom (early eviction of long prefixes). Two parallel asks: 1) can support provide one request_id from the customer for a failed request so we can pull the full trace? 2) can we quickly revert the canary routing while we root-cause?

emily-support: I asked customer for the request ids and they sent back one: rx-9f2a. Also they included curl with their headers and the exact system prompt. They are okay with a brief rollback while you investigate.

jonathan-r: I'll open a rollback PR to remove the fp16-optimized routing from canary immediately. @deploy-bot queue rollback.

deploy-bot: Rollback queued. Estimated 3 minutes to complete.

maria-l: Please make a customer-facing postmortem draft after we confirm root cause. For now, advise support to offer to roll back and credit for extra tokens due to retries. @emily-support, send the standard token-credit template.

eng-ml-oncall: Next steps for eng-ml: reproduce locally by sending a long system prompt similar to their 3.2k prompt against fp16-optimized kernel b1527 with kv_cache_max_seq artificially set to 2048. If we reproduce, check where prefix chunking threshold is applied and whether the fallback path shortens cached sequence length.

kevin-s: Quick mitigation: bump prefix_chunk threshold to force single-chunk path for the very long system prompts, and disable the automated fallback to attn-compat for canary until verified. I can ship a hotfix toggle to runtime config and we can re-enable once validated.

emily-support: Customer updated: they've seen the rollback start and appreciate the quick response. They also asked: is there a permanent fix timeline? I told them we'll follow up within 48 hours with next steps.

eng-ml-oncall: Good. After rollback and repro, we'll prepare a fix: either align kv_cache eviction to stable behavior or add explicit preservation of system prompt tokens in the cache policy. Will follow up with a short postmortem.

maria-l: Thanks team. Keep thread updated with any additional request_ids or odd headers.

emily-support: will do — I saved customer logs in the support ticket: TKT-14892 and emailed the tracing link to eng-ml. Closing in-thread unless new info comes in. :white_check_mark:
